what_changed: The read lane arms its release deadlines at the request rather than at the relay's own transport acknowledgment, so the acknowledgment latency of the outstation no longer sits inside the interval the master sees. The response budget is raised from 4 ms to 8 ms because request anchoring measures that deadline from the request and it must cover the relay's whole request-to-response latency. Diagnosis, implementation, and the before-and-after on the same hardware: defense4/timing/anchor_fix/FINDINGS.md.

hardware.switch_ctrl: ufispace / decps@10.10.54.81, Intel Tofino-1, SDE 9.13.2, bfrt_grpc localhost:50052

loaded_program.allocator: 12 ingress stages, 6 egress, critical path 12, 113 tables; the frozen parent is 12/6/12/112

config.shape_note: configure-all leaves shape=1; each block forces shape_set.py 0 and READS IT BACK, and aborts unless the readback says 0. campaign_v1 assumed it, which is why its configuration provenance is PARTIAL; this dataset's is not.
config.anchor_note: Each block also reads tbl_bor_params.anchor_req back from the switch and aborts unless it matches the arm. A block whose anchor state cannot be proved is a block whose capture cannot be attributed.

obfuscated_arm.budget_note: D_A + D_R = 28 ms is the smallest total on the 4 ms tick grid (A and R must be exact multiples of the 256 ns tick) that covers this relay's worst observed request-to-response latency, 24.691 ms over 6,288 Timing OFF exchanges measured 2026-09-18.

driver.guard: SELECT/OPERATE indices hard-restricted to {1,3}=RB02/RB04 (drive no relay output). Index 6/RB07/breaker-close refused at frame construction.
